extracted.intended_audience: users of the Singular computer algebra system (mathematicians, computational algebra researchers, and programmers using Singular)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for Singular kernel and library functions: syntax, types, purposes, examples, notes and restrictions for each function. Useful for implementing algebraic computations and scripting in Singular.

rubrics_metrics.name: char
rubrics_metrics.description: returns the characteristic of the coefficient field of a ring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: char(ring name). Type: int. Examples show char returns 0 for characteristic 0/fields like QQ or real, primes for finite fields, and base prime for prime-power rings (e.g. ring rp=(49,a) returns 7). See Section 5.1.7 [charstr] and 4.19 [ring].

rubrics_metrics.name: char_series
rubrics_metrics.description: the rows of the returned matrix represent the irreducible characteristic series of the ideal with respect to the current ordering of variables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: char_series(ideal expression). Type: matrix. One application is decomposition of the zero-set. Example: char_series(ideal(xyz,xz,y)) returns rows indicating characteristic series. See C.4 [Characteristic sets].

rubrics_metrics.name: charstr
rubrics_metrics.description: returns the description (string) of the coefficient field of a ring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: charstr(ring name). Type: string. Warning: tests for certain types; coefficients should use routines from ring.lib as the string representation may change. Examples: 'ZZ/32003', 'QQ', '7,a', 'Float()'. See char, ordstr, ring, ring lib, varstr.

rubrics_metrics.name: chinrem
rubrics_metrics.description: applies the Chinese Remainder Theorem to the first argument with respect to the moduli given in the second.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax variants: chinrem(list,intvec) etc. Type: same as elements of first argument. Elements must be all same type (bigint/int, poly, ideal, module or matrix); moduli must be bigint/int. If data depend on a ring, coefficient field must be Q. Works recursively on lists of lists. Examples show reconstruction of integers and ideals modulo moduli. See modstd lib.

rubrics_metrics.name: cleardenom
rubrics_metrics.description: multiplies a polynomial or vector by a suitable constant to cancel all denominators from its coefficients and then divides by its content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: cleardenom(poly|vector). Type: same as input. Examples show canceling denominators in polynomials and vectors. See content.

rubrics_metrics.name: close
rubrics_metrics.description: closes a link.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: close(link expression). Type: none. Example closes an ssi/tcp link to a Singular server. See link and open.

rubrics_metrics.name: coef
rubrics_metrics.description: determines monomials in a polynomial divisible by a specified product of ring variables and returns the monomials and their coefficients (as polynomials in remaining variables).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: coef(poly,product_of_ringvars) returning a 2×n matrix (monomials and coefficients). Also supports vector form filling provided matrices. coef returns only actually occurring monomials (no zero entries). Examples illustrate returned matrices. See coeffs for contrast.

rubrics_metrics.name: coeffs
rubrics_metrics.description: develops polynomials (or ideal/vector/module) as univariate in a given ring variable and returns coefficients as a matrix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many overloads: coeffs(poly, var), coeffs(ideal, var), coeffs(..., matrix name) and also coeffs(M,K,product_of_ringvars) expressing entries of M in K*A = M where K supplies monomials. Returns zero coefficients where monomials absent. Optional third argument returns matrix of powers. When K lacks needed monomials only a prefix of M is reproduced. Examples and notes describe shapes for polynomials, ideals, vectors, modules; optional product_of_ringvars picks the variable (default x=1). See coef and kbase.

rubrics_metrics.name: contract
rubrics_metrics.description: contracts each element of the second ideal by each element of the first ideal, producing an m×n matrix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: contract(ideal I, ideal J). Type: matrix. Contraction defined on monomials by contract(x^A,x^B): x^(B−A) if B≥A componentwise else 0; extended bilinearly. Example provided. See diff.

rubrics_metrics.name: crossprod
rubrics_metrics.description: cross product of several cring objects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: crossprod(cring expression,...). Type: cring. Example: crossprod(ZZ/32003,Float()) yields 'ZZ/32003 x Float()'. See cring section.

rubrics_metrics.name: datetime
rubrics_metrics.description: returns the current date and time as a string.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure from standard.lib. Syntax: datetime(). Return: string. Example output format shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: dbprint
rubrics_metrics.description: applies print to each expression in a list if a given integer expression (debug flag) is positive; also applies print if printlevel>=voice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax variants: dbprint(int, expression list) or dbprint(expression). Type: none. Used to conditionally display messages during procedures. Example demonstrates debug variable controlling printing. See libraries, debugging tools, print-level, voice, print.

rubrics_metrics.name: defined
rubrics_metrics.description: returns non-zero (TRUE) if a user-defined object with given name exists, 0 otherwise; non-zero value indicates the level where object is defined (-1 for ring variables/constants).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: defined(name). Type: int. Returned value: level (1 top-level, 2 first-level procedure, etc.) or -1 for ring variables/constants. Example usage includes comparing to voice to check current-level definition. See rvar and voice.

rubrics_metrics.name: deg
rubrics_metrics.description: returns the maximal (weighted) degree of terms of a polynomial or a vector; deg(0) is -1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: deg(poly|vector) with optional intvec weight vector. Default weights: 1 for lex/block orderings; base ring default weights for single-block orderings. Type: int. Examples show behavior with weighted orderings. See jet, ord, poly, vector.

rubrics_metrics.name: degree
rubrics_metrics.description: computes (prints) the (Krull) dimension and multiplicity of the ideal or module generated by the leading monomials of the input; equals dimension and multiplicity of input if it is a standard basis w.r.t. a degree ordering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: degree(ideal|module). Type: string. Useful on std basis; example shows usage with std(jacob(f)). See dim, mult, std, vdim.

rubrics_metrics.name: delete
rubrics_metrics.description: deletes element with given index from a list/intvec/ideal/module (does not change original).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: delete(container, int). Type: same as first argument. Examples show deleting from list and int range and from ideal (maxideal). See insert, intvec, list, module, ideal.

rubrics_metrics.name: denominator
rubrics_metrics.description: returns the denominator of a number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: denominator(number expression). Type: number. Example: denominator(3/2) → 2. See cleardenom, content, numerator.

rubrics_metrics.name: det
rubrics_metrics.description: returns determinant of a square matrix (module considered as matrix).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: det(intmat|matrix|module). Type: int or poly depending on input. Algorithms depend on input type: Bareiss algorithm for symbolic entries; Chinese remainder algorithm otherwise. For large sparse problems using module input can be advantageous. Example given. See intmat, matrix, minor.

rubrics_metrics.name: diff
rubrics_metrics.description: computes partial derivative of polynomial objects by a ring variable, or differentiates polynomials of second ideal by differential operators given by first ideal (producing m×n matrix); can differentiate numbers (rational functions) by transcendental ring parameters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: many overloads: diff(poly,var), diff(vector,var), diff(ideal,var), diff(module,var), diff(matrix,var), diff(ideal,ideal) (matrix output), diff(number, ring parameter). Type: same as first argument (except matrix for ideal-ideal). Examples include differentiation of polynomials, vectors, ideal-by-ideal yielding a matrix, and differentiation of rational functions when coefficient ring is transcendental extension. See contract, ideal, jacob, matrix, module, poly, var, vector.

rubrics_metrics.name: dim
rubrics_metrics.description: computes the dimension (Krull dimension) of the ideal/module generated by leading monomials of given generators, or cohomological dimension for resolution objects; dim(I,J) is dimension of I/J.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: dim(ideal|module|resolution) and variants with second ideal. Type: int. Returns -1 for ideal(1). Examples and notes: dimension of module is dimension of its annihilator; for standard bases dimension equals that of ideal. See degree, ideal, mult, std, vdim.

rubrics_metrics.name: division
rubrics_metrics.description: computes a division with remainder for ideals or modules; returns list [T,R,U] where T is matrix, R ideal/module (remainder), U diagonal matrix of units satisfying matrix(M)*U = matrix(N)*T + matrix(R).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: division(M,N) and variants with truncation degree n and weight vector w. Uses different algorithms depending on whether N is a standard basis. For polynomial baserings U=identity. Additional args allow truncated standard representations up to weighted degree n w.r.t. w (default w = ones). Returns standard representation for normal form. See lift, module, poly operations, reduce. Examples show outputs and warnings when input is not a standard basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: dump
rubrics_metrics.description: writes the state of the Singular session (all defined variables and their values) to a specified link in ASCII or ssi format so getdump can retrieve it later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: dump(link expression). Type: none. Restrictions: for ASCII links integer matrices in lists are dumped as integer list elements (not matrices) and lists of lists are flattened; links themselves are not dumped. Example shows writing to and reading from dump.ascii and many 'redefining' messages. See getdump, link, write.

rubrics_metrics.name: eliminate
rubrics_metrics.description: eliminates variables occurring as factors/entries of second argument from an ideal (resp. submodule) by intersecting it with subring not containing these variables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: eliminate(ideal|module, product_of_ringvars or intvec, optional intvec hilb). Does not need special ordering nor a standard basis as input. For homogeneous input, computing Hilbert function first (fast ordering e.g. dp) can speed computation: provide intvec from hilb(std(j),1) for Hilbert-driven elimination. If ideal/module not homogeneous with weights 1, intvec ignored. Examples given. See hilb, ideal, module, std.

rubrics_metrics.name: eval
rubrics_metrics.description: evaluates (quoted) expressions; within a quoted expression each eval undoes exactly one quote.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: eval(expression). Type: none. Used when receiving quoted expressions from ssi links along with quote and write to prevent local evaluations when writing to ssi link. Example demonstrates writing quoted std(eval(i+j)) to ssi and later read+evaluate. See Ssi links, quote, write.

rubrics_metrics.name: ERROR
rubrics_metrics.description: immediately interrupts current computation, returns to top-level, and displays the argument string as error message.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: ERROR(string expression). Type: none. Intended for emergency/failure exits within procedures. Example shows that variables set after ERROR are not reached; message and 'leaving ::proc' printed.

rubrics_metrics.name: example
rubrics_metrics.description: computes an example for a given topic; examples are available for all Singular kernel and library functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: example topic. Purpose: demonstrate usage of kernel/library functions. Use TAB completion (where available) to list example topics. Examples: example prime; example intvec_declarations. See help.

rubrics_metrics.name: execute
rubrics_metrics.description: executes a string containing a sequence of Singular commands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: execute(string). Type: none. Note: the command return cannot appear in the string. execute should be avoided in procedures because it may give rise to name conflicts and prevents precompilation. Example: constructing string from read file and execute to define ideal k.

rubrics_metrics.name: extgcd
rubrics_metrics.description: computes extended gcd: returns list [g, s, t] with g = gcd(a,b) and s,t such that g = a*s + b*t.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: extgcd for int, bigint or univariate poly arguments. Type: list of 3 objects of same argument type. Note: polynomials must be univariate in same variable. Examples for integers and polynomials. See gcd, int.

rubrics_metrics.name: facstd
rubrics_metrics.description: returns a list of ideals computed by the factorizing Groebner basis algorithm; intersection of these ideals has same zero-set (radical) as input.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: facstd(ideal) or facstd(ideal,constraints). Type: list of ideals. The second optional argument gives polynomials defining non-zero constraints: ideals containing a constraint polynomial are omitted from output. Not implemented for baserings over real ground fields and galois fields of type (p^n,a). Examples show factorization into components. See ring and std.

rubrics_metrics.name: factmodd
rubrics_metrics.description: computes a factorization of a polynomial h(x,y) in K[[x]][y] up to a certain degree in x using Hensel-lifting, given factorization of h(0,y) or computing it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: factmodd(h,d,[f0,g0],[xIndex,yIndex],[..]). Type: list of polys. Purpose: construct factors f(x,y), g(x,y) modulo x^(d+1) when h(0,y) splits into two co-prime monic factors f0,g0. If f0,g0 missing algorithm factors h(0,y) and expects exactly two distinct factors. xIndex,yIndex default to 1,2. Input h must be in K[x,y] and ring must have at least two variables. Example given and reduce check. See factorize.

rubrics_metrics.name: factorize
rubrics_metrics.description: computes irreducible factors of a polynomial, optionally with multiplicities or excluding constants depending on second argument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: factorize(poly [,mode]) where mode 0 returns factors and multiplicities (first factor constant), 1 returns non-constant factors (no multiplicities), 2 returns non-constant factors with multiplicities. Type: list of ideal and intvec / ideal depending on mode. Not implemented for coefficient fields real, finite fields of type (p^n,a) and ZZ/m. Examples show factorization over finite prime fields and splitting behavior over extensions. See absFactorize and poly.

rubrics_metrics.name: farey
rubrics_metrics.description: lifts integers (or other objects) modulo B to rationals via Farey rational reconstruction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: farey(bigint, bigint) and overloads for ideals/modules/matrices/lists. Type: type of first argument (unless list). Purpose: returns a/b as best approximation satisfying bounds |a|,|b| <= sqrt((N−1)/2) condition (text in page partly garbled). Requires current coefficient field QQ. Example: farey(2,32003) -> 2. See chinrem.

rubrics_metrics.name: fetch
rubrics_metrics.description: maps objects between rings: position-based mapping of variables/parameters; convenient for renaming/reordering or mapping to/from quotient rings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: fetch(ring name, name [, intvec permutation [, intvec param_mapping]]). Type: number, poly, vector, ideal, module, matrix, or list depending on second argument. fetch is identity between rings and qrings using i-th variable mapping. If destination has fewer variables extra source variables map to zero. intvec describes permutation mapping; negative numbers and fourth arg describe mapping of parameters; zero maps variable to 0. Coefficient fields must be compatible (see map). fetch uses positions not names (contrast with imap). Examples show mapping polynomials, vectors, ideals between rings and qrings. See imap, map, qring, ring.

rubrics_metrics.name: fglm
rubrics_metrics.description: computes for given ideal in a given ring a reduced Groebner basis in the current ring using the FGLM algorithm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: fglm(ring name, ideal name). Type: ideal. Purpose: main application is computing a lexicographical Groebner basis from a reduced Groebner basis w.r.t. a degree ordering; often much faster than direct lex computation. Assumes the ideal is zero-dimensional and given as a reduced Groebner basis in given ring; monomial ordering must be global. Only permissible differences between given ring and current ring are monomial ordering and permutation of variables/parameters.
